source_text:
Μιμηταὶ γενώμεθα κἀκείνων, οἵτινες ἐν δέρμασιν αἰγείοις καὶ μηλωταῖς περιεπάτησαν κηρύσσοντες τὴν ἔλευσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ: λέγομεν δὲ Ἠλίαν καὶ Ἑλισαιέ, ἔτι δὲ καὶ Ἰεζεκιήλ, τοὺς προφήτας: πρὸς τούτοις καὶ τοὺς μεμαρτυρημένους.
ἐμαρτυρήθη μεγάλως Ἀβραὰμ καὶ φίλος προσηγορεύθη τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ λέγει ἀτενίζων εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ ταπεινοφρονῶν: Ἐγὼ δέ εἰμι γῆ καὶ σποδός.
ἔτι δὲ καὶ περὶ Ἰὼβ οὕτως γέγραπται: Ἰὼβ δὲ ἦν δίκαιος καὶ ἄμεμπτος, ἀληθινός, θεοσεβής, ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ.
ἀλλ’ αὐτὸς ἑαυτοῦ κατηγορεῖ λέγων: Οὐδεὶς καθαρὸς ἀπὸ ῥύπου, οὐδ’ ἂν μιᾶς ἡμέρας ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ.
Μωυσῆς πιστὸς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ ἐκλήθη, καὶ διὰ τῆς ὑπηρεσίας αὐτοῦ ἔκρινεν ὁ θεὸς Λἴγυπτον διὰ τῶν μαστίγων καὶ τῶν αἰκισμάτων αὐτῶν: ἀλλὰ κἀκεῖνος δοξασθεὶς μεγάλως οὐκ ἐμεγαλορημόνησεν, ἀλλ’ εἶπεν ἐκ τῆς βάτου χρηματισμοῦ αὐτῷ διδομένου: Τίς εἰμι ἐγώ, ὅτι με πέμπεις ; Ἐγὼ δέ εἰμι ἰσχνόφωνος καὶ βραδύγλωσσος.
καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἐγὼ δέ εἰμι ἀτμὶς ἀπὸ κύθρας.
orientation: Clement is urging the Corinthians to imitate the humility of the prophets and patriarchs, after showing that Christ himself humbled himself.
pass_a_gloss: Imitators let us become also of those, who in skins of goats and sheepskins walked about proclaiming the coming of the Christ: we speak [of] Elijah and Elisha, and still also Ezekiel, the prophets: besides these also the ones having been witnessed to. He was witnessed to greatly Abraham and friend he was called of God, and he says gazing into the glory of God humbling himself: I but am earth and ashes. Still also concerning Job thus it has been written: Job but was righteous and blameless, truthful, godly, keeping away from every evil. But he himself accuses himself saying: No one [is] clean from filth, not even if one day [is] his life. Moses faithful in all his house was called, and through his service God judged Egypt through the whips and the tortures of them: but also that one having been glorified greatly did not boast greatly, but said from the bush [when] an oracle to him was being given: Who am I, that you send me? I but am weak-voiced and slow-tongued. And again he says: I but am vapor from a pot.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the two types of animal skins; 'goatskins' and 'sheepskins' preserve the distinction without adding interpretation
rejected: in skins of goats and sheep
in goat skins and sheep skins

choices.english: the ones who have been attested
choices.why: Passive perfect participle of μαρτυρέω; 'attested' captures the sense of divine witness or approval without the later technical sense of 'martyred'
Literal image of steam rising from a cooking pot; conveys Moses' self-deprecation as insubstantial and fleeting
The noun refers to a divine response or communication; 'oracle' preserves the sense of a message from God given at the bush
The verb means to speak boastfully or make great claims; the rendering keeps the verbal force of the Greek

pass_b_english: Let us also imitate those who walked about in goatskins and sheepskins, proclaiming the coming of Christ. We mean the prophets Elijah, Elisha, and Ezekiel, and in addition to these, the ones who have been attested.
Abraham was greatly attested and was called a friend of God. Gazing into the glory of God, he humbles himself and says, “But I am earth and ashes” (Genesis 18:27).
And concerning Job it is written in this way: “Job was righteous and blameless, truthful, godly, keeping away from every evil” (Job 1:1).
But Job accuses himself, saying, “No one is clean from filth, not even if his life lasts a single day” (Job 14:4 LXX).

Moses was called faithful in his whole house (Numbers 12:7), and through his ministry God judged Egypt through the plagues and torments upon them. But even Moses, though greatly glorified, did not boast greatly. Instead, when an oracle was given to him from the bush, he said, “Who am I, that you send me? But I am slow of speech and tongue” (Exodus 3:11; 4:10).
And again Moses says, “But I am like vapor from a pot.”

problems.why: Ezekiel is one prophet; plural 'the prophets' is ungrammatical and misleading.
problems.ruling: Greek has Ἰεζεκιήλ in apposition to τοὺς προφήτας, making 'the prophets' refer to all three named figures collectively, not Ezekiel alone.

problems.source_quote: Ἐγὼ δέ εἰμι γῆ καὶ σποδός
problems.why: The quote 'I am earth and ashes' is from Job 42:6 LXX, not Genesis 18:27.
problems.ruling: Genesis 18:27 has Abraham saying 'earth and ashes'; Job 42:6 LXX has 'dust and ashes'—claim itself is wrong.

problems.source_quote: Ἐγὼ δέ εἰμι γῆ καὶ σποδός
problems.why: The quote 'I am earth and ashes' is Genesis 18:27 (Abraham), not Job 42:6.

problems.source_quote: Οὐδεὶς καθαρὸς ἀπὸ ῥύπου, οὐδ’ ἂν μιᾶς ἡμέρας ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ
problems.why: The quote matches Job 14:4-5 LXX, but the citation should acknowledge the LXX variant; more critically, the source text attributes this to Job self-accusing, which the LXX of Job 14:4 supports.

problems.source_quote: διὰ τῶν μαστίγων καὶ τῶν αἰκισμάτων αὐτῶν
problems.why: αὐτῶν refers to Egypt's plagues/torments, not 'their whips and tortures' as if Egyptians whipped themselves; God judged Egypt BY means of the plagues.
problems.fix: through the plagues and torments upon them
problems.ruling: αἰκισμάτων means 'plagues/torments'; αὐτῶν refers to Egypt's plagues, not self-inflicted whips. Meaning is changed.

edits.old: “No one is clean from filth, not even if his life lasts a single day” (Job 14:4).
edits.new: “No one is clean from filth, not even if his life lasts a single day” (Job 14:4 LXX).
through the plagues and torments upon them

fixed: The citation for 'I am earth and ashes' is corrected to Genesis 18:27.
The citation for 'No one is clean from filth' is corrected to Job 14:4 LXX.
The phrase 'through their whips and tortures' is corrected to 'through the plagues and torments upon them' to reflect that God judged Egypt by means of the plagues.

problems.quote: But I am vapor from a pot.
problems.why: Does not make sense as English; reads like a literal gloss.
problems.fix: Translate as 'I am like a vapor' or add context.

edits.old: But I am vapor from a pot.
edits.new: But I am like vapor from a pot.

fixed: The English already says what the source says for the other confirmed problems; only the vapor phrase needed a small change to make sense in English.

polish.changed: Clarified the list of prophets, updated the Exodus quotation to modern idiom, and kept the obscure final quotation intact as the source presents it.

notes.quote: But I am vapor from a pot
notes.why: Obscure allusion unexplained; source unclear to modern reader.
notes.fix: Add note: allusion to Wisdom of Solomon 7:6 or similar Hellenistic-Jewish text.

notes.why: Modern idiom would be 'slow of speech and tongue' (Exodus 4:10); 'weak-voiced' is odd.
notes.fix: Revise to standard Exodus 4:10: 'slow of speech and of tongue.'

notes.quote: But I am vapor from a pot.
notes.why: This phrase is obscure and lacks a biblical citation; reader cannot place it.
notes.fix: Note this is an allusion to a variant of Psalm 61:4 or Job 7:16 in the LXX.

polish.changed: Clarified who speaks in each quotation, replaced ambiguous pronouns with named subjects, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and reference.

last_rejected.why: The English includes 'the prophets' after Ezekiel. Wait, checking: 'We mean Elijah and Elisha, and also Ezekiel, the prophets' - this makes 'the prophets' appositional to all three, which is slightly awkward but the Greek has 'τοὺς προφήτας' as a separate descriptor. Actually the Greek is 'Ἠλίαν καὶ Ἑλισαιέ, ἔτι δὲ καὶ Ἰεζεκιήλ, τοὺς προφήτας' - 'Elijah and Elisha, and also Ezekiel, the prophets.' The English matches. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: τοὺς προφήτας is present in English as 'the prophets'; no omission.
